title: Heritage designation deadline extension request to province
subtitle: Year-end budget reports, election compliance committee, 2030 voting methods, and an offer on 170 Stephanie Drive for housing.
overview: Council asked the Province of Ontario to extend the January 1, 2027 deadline for issuing notices of intent to designate properties listed on municipal heritage registers, suggesting January 1, 2030 or another reasonable timeframe {{vote:m9}}. Staff said the current timeline is close to impossible for the large number of listed properties still to be reviewed. Some councillors opposed the request, saying the province has already given enough time.

A consent report passed without debate. It set up a joint election compliance audit committee for 2026-2030 and allocated the 2025 operating surpluses and deficits to reserves. It also approved capital budget adjustments, an updated Development Charge Exemptions Policy, and a direction to consider home-voting methods for the 2030 election.

After a closed session, the Mayor announced that Council has made an offer on the lands known as 170 Stephanie Drive to increase the supply of permanent affordable and attainable housing. Council also gave direction to staff on two Ontario Land Tribunal matters. The minutes report no further detail on those matters.

decisions.detail: Council asked the Province to extend the January 1, 2027 deadline for notices of intent to designate listed heritage properties, possibly to 2030, and to circulate the request widely {{vote:m9}}.
Council established a joint Municipal Election Compliance Audit Committee for 2026-2030 and delegated member appointments and Terms of Reference updates to the City Clerk.
Council allocated the 2025 tax-supported and non-tax-supported results to and from reserves and approved a $175,000 increase to the 2026 operating budget for an HR job evaluation system.
Council approved 2025 and 2026 capital budget adjustments, for a net increase of $1,732,242 to the 2026 capital budget.

decisions.item: Reserves, debt and development charge exemptions
decisions.detail: Council received the long-term financial statement, approved an updated Development Charge Exemptions Policy and DC exemption reserve funds, and moved $2,000,000 from the Fire sick leave reserve to the WSIB reserve.
Council directed the City Clerk to prioritize voting methods that let voters mark a ballot independently at home and to report back in 2028.

debate: Supporters of the heritage request said staff are working hard on voluntary designations, at-risk properties and conservation districts, and that specialized planners are hard to find. They noted that a property that falls off the register generally cannot be added back for several years.

Staff said more than 1,800 listed properties remain to be reviewed and that the current timeline makes this close to impossible. They supported more time. Staff also said other heritage work, such as updating a registry, has been paused, and a potentially significant historic home has already been approved for demolition.

One councillor opposed the request on behalf of homeowners who want certainty, citing stress over home insurance and replacement costs. That councillor noted that voluntary designation is already available and that the province gave a long lead time.

A supporter said insurance concerns have largely been resolved through staff work with owners. This councillor pointed to owner support for the downtown heritage district and to earlier funding proposals to speed up the work.
Another opposing view held that the province already granted one extension and that a firm deadline brings certainty. This councillor doubted the province would act on the request.
